'''Jason Alan Kapono''' (kah-POH-noh; born February 2, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was the first [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player to lead the league in [[three-point field goal percentage]] in two consecutive seasons, and also won the [[Three-Point Contest]] twice (2007, 2008). He won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Miami Heat]] in [[2006 NBA Finals|2006]].

Kapono played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He was the first player in the school's history to earn first-team [[All-Pac-10 men's basketball team|All-Pac-10]] honors for four years and was also the first UCLA player to lead the team in scoring four straight years. Kapono began his NBA career with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], who drafted him in the second round of the [[2003 NBA draft]]. He later played in the NBA for the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]], Miami, [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] before joining [[Panathinaikos B.C.]] in Greece.

==Early life==
Kapono was born in [[Long Beach, California]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors Sign Jason Kapono to Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-jason-kapono-contract |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jason Kapono - All Things Lakers - Los Angeles Times |url=https://projects.latimes.com/lakers/player/jason-kapono/ |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=projects.latimes.com |language=en}}</ref> to Joe and Joni Kapono. Jason prepped at Southern California basketball powerhouse [[Artesia High School (Lakewood, California)|Artesia High School]] in [[Lakewood, California]], where he was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and won several accolades and titles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Jason Kapono|work=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208185153|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407085202/http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208185153|archive-date=April 7, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> In his senior year at Artesia he averaged 23.5 points and 9.0 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketba/99allusab.htm|title=Harvey named national player of the year|access-date=2012-04-13|date=1999-05-21|work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

After a successful high school career, he enjoyed an outstanding college career at [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], where he finished as the third all-time leading scorer with 2,095 points, was the first Bruin to earn first-team [[All-Pac-10 men's basketball team|All-Pac-10]] honors all four years, and was the only UCLA player to lead the school in scoring four straight years.<ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA Bruins in the NBA (2011) |work=UclaBruins.com |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/ucla-m-baskbl-nbabruins.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120829163105/http://www.uclabruins.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/ucla-m-baskbl-nbabruins.html |archive-date=August 29, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also set a school record for most [[three-point field goal|three-pointers]] made in a game when he connected on 9 of 11 attempts against [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] on January 4, [[2002–03 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2003]].{{#tag:ref|The record was tied by [[Bryce Alford]] when he made 9 of 11 on March 19, [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2015]].<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 14-seed UAB (20-15) vs. No. 11-seed UCLA (21-13)|date=March 21, 2015|publisher=UCLA Sports Information|url=https://www.nmnathletics.com//pdf9/3321319.pdf?SPSID=749897&SPID=126928&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=30500|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222162155/https://www.nmnathletics.com//pdf9/3321319.pdf?SPSID=749897&SPID=126928&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=30500|archive-date=December 22, 2015|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all|access-date=March 22, 2015}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} Kapono graduated with a degree in history. He was a second-round draft choice of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2003 NBA draft]].<ref name=76ers_bio>{{cite web|title=2010–11 Sixers Media Guide |pages=71–3 |year=2010 |publisher=Philadelphia 76ers |work=NBA.com |url=http://mediacentral.nba.com/media/mediacentral/2010-11-Sixers.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407090430/http://mediacentral.nba.com/media/mediacentral/2010-11-Sixers.pdf |archive-date=April 7, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Professional career==
{{BLP sources section|date=July 2022}}

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2004) ===
Kapono only played 41 games and started 3 in his first NBA season, although he led the team in three-point field goal percent at .477, averaging 3.5 PPG for his rookie season. He became an efficient 3-point shooter and was also good from the free-throw line, shooting 83%. The Cavaliers finished the season 37–45 and missed [[2004 NBA playoffs|the playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003-04 Cleveland Cavaliers Roster and Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CLE/2004.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112010738/https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CLE/2004.html |archive-date=2020-11-12 |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Charlotte Bobcats (2004–2005) ===
After his rookie season with Cleveland, he was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in the [[2004 NBA expansion draft|2004 expansion draft]], where he increased his scoring average from 3.5 to 8.5 points per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jason Kapono NBA & ABA Statistics {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com |url=http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kaponja01.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101204124405/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/kaponja01.html |archive-date=2010-12-04 |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=www.basketball-reference.com}}</ref> He also made the first block in Bobcats history. Kapono also increased his assist and rebound average this season, although his total FG%, including his 3P%, slightly declined. This was the Bobcats first ever season and the team was very young and had potential, although they were very inexperienced.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Bobcats Become NBA’s 30th Team {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/official_team.html |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> The Bobcats finished the season with an 18–64 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2004-05 Charlotte Bobcats |url=http://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CHA/2005_games.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623141534/http://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CHA/2005_games.html |archive-date=2016-06-23 |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Kapono was a free agent by the offseason, but the Bobcats decided to not re-sign him.

=== Miami Heat (2005–2007) ===
Kapono was signed as a free agent by the [[Miami Heat]] where he was part of the [[2005–06 Miami Heat season|2005–06 championship team]]. His scoring took a toll as he had a lesser role on the team, dropping down to 4.1 for the season, playing just 51 games in the season. Kapono won his first and only championship with the Heat during the [[2006 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 NBA Finals - Heat vs. Mavericks |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/2006-nba-finals-heat-vs-mavericks.html |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Kapono's points-per-game average and minutes played significantly increased, and he [[List of National Basketball Association annual three-point field goal percentage leaders|led the league in three-point percentage]] with .514, coming close to the all-time single-season three-point percentage record held by [[Kyle Korver]] (.536), and is the fourth best percentage in league season history. He averaged a career high in scoring, minutes, and rebounding. Kapono also won the [[Three-Point Contest]] in the [[2007 NBA All-Star Game|2007 All-Star Game]] three-point shoot-out competition by defeating [[Dirk Nowitzki]] and [[Gilbert Arenas]] in the final round with a score of 24 points, tying [[Mark Price]]'s record for most points in a final round of the three-point contest. The 2006–07 season is greatly considered to be the best season of his career due to his accomplishments and statistics. Despite this, the defending champions had a disappointing season, finishing with an average 44–38 record and getting swept in the first round by the [[Chicago Bulls]].

=== Toronto Raptors (2007–2009) ===
[[File:Jason Kapono.JPG|thumb|upright|Kapono with the Raptors in 2007]]
Kapono became a free agent in the 2007 offseason and signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on July 11. His statistic averages went down following the 2006–07 season with the Heat, but he still played well. Kapono led the league in three-point percentage going into the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game|2008 All-Star Game]]. In the final round of the contest, he scored 25 points, tying the all-time single round record set in 1986 and also setting a new finals record.<ref>McMenamin, Dave, [http://www.nba.com/allstar2008/features/saturday_20080216.html "Kapono Lights Up Saturday Night"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090323112354/http://www.nba.com/allstar2008/features/saturday_20080216.html |date=March 23, 2009 }}, nba.com, February 17, 2008, accessed February 18, 2008.</ref> On December 14, 2007, he had a career-high 29 points and pulled down 8 rebounds. He also ended the 2007–08 season as the top three-point shooter in the league.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/statistics/player/3PointS.jsp?league=00&season=22007&conf=OVERALL&position=0&splitType=9&splitScope=GAME&qualified=Y&yearsExp=-1&splitDD= 2007–08 THREE POINTERS LEADERS:  3-Point FG Percentage] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081006165714/http://www.nba.com/statistics/player/3PointS.jsp?league=00&season=22007&conf=OVERALL&position=0&splitType=9&splitScope=GAME&qualified=Y&yearsExp=-1&splitDD= |date=October 6, 2008 }}, nba.com, accessed August 26, 2008.</ref> He was the first player in NBA history to have the highest three-point percentage in two consecutive seasons.<ref>{{cite news|last=Herring |first=Chris |title=Offense? Yes. Defense? Not So Much |date=December 18, 2012 |newspaper=The Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887323723104578185380145416440 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130209135909/http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887323723104578185380145416440.html |archive-date=February 9, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> He helped the Raptors reach the [[2008 NBA playoffs|2008 playoffs]]. The team finished the season with a 41–41 record and placed 6th in the East and faced an up-and-coming Orlando Magic team who beat the Raptors 4–1. Later in the summer, Kapono was picked for the [[USA Basketball]] Select Team which trained with USA Men's Senior National Team in [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]] to assist in the buildup to the [[2008 Summer Olympics]]. In the 2008–2009 season the Raptors missed the playoffs with a mediocre 33–49 record.

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2009–2011) ===
On June 9, 2009, Kapono was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for [[Reggie Evans]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/090609_Kapono.html Philadelphia 76ers Acquire Forward Jason Kapono From Toronto], nba.com accessed June 15, 2009.</ref> Kapono was a victim of several starting lineup changes throughout the season. Kapono started the season with sparing minutes off the bench, but was later given the starting SF spot, near the end of the season. However, after losing his starting spot two games into the following season, Kapono was back to coming off the bench for sparing minutes. The team finished with an abysmal record for the 2009–10 season, going 27–55. The 76ers made the playoffs in 2011, but were outmatched by Kapono's former team, the Miami Heat. They lost the series 1–4, with Kapono averaging 0.7 PPG for that season and didn't make an appearance of the [[2011 NBA playoffs|2011 playoffs]]. After the [[2010–11 NBA season]] came to an end, Kapono's contract with the 76ers expired and he became a free agent.<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Brian |title=Offseason shopping list: Thunder |date=June 21, 2011 |work=FOXSportsSouthwest.com |url=http://www.foxsportssouthwest.com/06/21/11/Offseason-shopping-list-Thunder/landing_thunder.html?blockID=533903&feedID=3799 |access-date=July 7, 2011 |quote=Jason Kapono is by far the best shooter in the free agent bunch, making treys at a 44 percent clip during his NBA career. }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Lakers (2011–2012) ===
On December 9, 2011, Kapono signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/111209lakerssignkapono.html Lakers sign Kapono]</ref> He only played 27 games for the Lakers. Kapono's final NBA game was played on March 14, 2012, in a 107–101 win over the [[New Orleans Hornets]] where he played for four minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 assist.

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2012) ===
On March 15, 2012, Kapono, along with [[Luke Walton]] and a 2012 first-round draft pick, were traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for [[Ramon Sessions]] and [[Christian Eyenga]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Cavaliers Acquire 2012 First Round Pick, Kapono, Walton and Right To Swap 2013 First Round Picks From Lakers | url = http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/trade_120315.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = March 15, 2012 | access-date = March 15, 2012}}</ref> He didn't play any games for the Cavaliers and was waived 2 days later on March 17.<ref>{{cite web | title = Cavaliers Announce Player Transactions | url = http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/harris_120317.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = March 17, 2012 | access-date = March 17, 2012}}</ref>

=== Retirement ===
Kapono reportedly retired in May 2014.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/121016/jason-kapono-retires-at-33.html Jason Kapono retires at 33]</ref> However, on October 4, 2014, he signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-jason-kapono-contract Warriors Sign Jason Kapono to Contract]</ref> He was later waived by the Warriors on October 24, 2014, after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Waive Craft, Kapono, Kilpatrick, Mcadoo and Watt|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/five-players-waived-20141024|access-date=October 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2014}}</ref> Kapono never played in the NBA again.

===NBA record===
At one point, Kapono was the most accurate three-point shooter in NBA history. On November 25, 2007, he made his 250th three-point shot, qualifying him for the NBA record in 3-point shooting accuracy. He immediately moved into first place with a .461 ratio of 3-point shots made to shots attempted, moving ahead of [[Steve Kerr]], who had the previous lifetime best at .454. Kapono has since dropped behind Kerr and others.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/statistics/default_all_time_leaders/AllTimeLeadersFG3PQuery.html?topic=4&stat=6 All Time Leaders: Three Point Field Goal Percentage] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303220725/http://www.nba.com/statistics/default_all_time_leaders/AllTimeLeadersFG3PQuery.html?topic=4&stat=6 |date=March 3, 2009 }}, nba.com, accessed January 31, 2008.</ref>

==Personal life==
Kapono is of [[Native Hawaiians|Hawaiian]] and [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] descent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Q&A |work=UCLABruins.com |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208183768 |access-date=January 17, 2014 |quote=And no I'm not Italian. I have no Italian in me. I have some Hawaiian and Portuguese, but no Italian. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006102720/http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208183768 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }}</ref> He has a sister, Jillian.
